query: Review pr-triage.yml in this directory. It is one of our GitHub Actions workflows. Tell me exactly what is wrong with it and show the fixed YAML.
expected_behavior: Flags script injection: the ${{ github.event.issue.title }} and ${{ github.event.comment.body }} expressions are pasted into the run: shell before it executes, so an attacker-chosen title or comment body becomes commands

Fixes the injection by moving each untrusted expression into env: and referencing the quoted shell variable (for example TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }} then echo "$TITLE"), not by escaping or sanitising the expression in place
Requires third-party actions to be pinned to a full 40-character commit SHA with a trailing version comment, and flags at least peter-evans/create-or-update-comment@v4 as a mutable tag
Requires an explicit least-privilege permissions: block, notes that a workflow with no permissions: inherits the repository default, and scopes write scopes to the individual jobs that need them

Identifies the pull_request_target job checking out ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} and then running npm ci && npm test as a pwn request: fork-controlled code and lifecycle scripts execute with a write token and the repository secrets

Recommends the privilege-separation fix for that job — run the untrusted code under the plain pull_request trigger and consume only its output from a privileged workflow_run or pull_request_target job — instead of merely adding permissions
Flags that AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are long-lived secrets reachable from this externally triggerable workflow and recommends OIDC with id-token: write instead

query: pr-notes.md in this directory is my draft description. I am on branch fix/cache-key, the base is our release/2.x branch, and this work closes issue #412. Walk me through opening the pull request with the gh CLI and then handling the review round.
expected_behavior: Warns that closing keywords such as Closes #412 are ignored when the pull request does not target the repository default branch, so a PR onto release/2.x will not auto-close #412 and the issue must be linked another way
Passes the body through a file with gh pr create --body-file (and --base release/2.x) rather than an inline --body string, because the multi-line markdown body breaks under shell escaping

Rewrites the description as a reviewer-facing cover note: keeps the root cause (header casing normalised after hashing), the where-to-start pointer and the breaking-change note, and drops the file list, the pasted npm test output and the checklist
Reviews the whole branch against the base before writing the description (gh pr diff, or git diff base...HEAD) instead of trusting the draft notes

Replies to inline review comments on their own thread — POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments/{id}/replies, or the equivalent GraphQL thread reply — rather than posting a new top-level PR comment
Uses gh pr checks (with --watch) or gh run view --log-failed to get the actual CI failure before changing code

query: CODEOWNERS-draft in this directory is the CODEOWNERS file I am about to commit. I want code owners to actually gate merges on our main branch and I want direct pushes to main blocked. Check the file and tell me what to configure on the repository.
expected_behavior: Flags that ! negation (!/src/**/generated/**) is not supported in CODEOWNERS even though it works in gitignore, and that the line is skipped rather than excluding anything
Flags that character-range patterns like [Dd]ocs/ are not supported in CODEOWNERS, so the docs rule never matches
Explains that the last matching pattern wins, so /src/** placed after /src/ui/ takes ownership of src/ui files back from @acme/web, and reorders general patterns before specific ones
Flags that repeating /src/ui/ on two lines silently keeps only the last owner (@jsmith) and that co-owners must be listed on one line
States that CODEOWNERS only gates merges when required reviews plus require review from Code Owners is enabled on the branch (ruleset or branch protection) — the file alone does nothing

Notes that the file must live on the base branch of the pull request (.github/, repo root or docs/) and that every listed user or team needs write access to the repository or the owner is silently dropped
Gives a concrete way to apply the branch rules, such as gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets with a branch ruleset that requires a pull request and code-owner review and blocks direct pushes

Warns that any pre-existing branch protection rule on main keeps applying alongside the new ruleset, that rulesets have no priority and aggregate so the most restrictive version of a shared rule wins, and that the existing protection must therefore be read (for example gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection) before claiming what is enforced

query: I want to squash my last three commits into one and rewrite the commit message. What is the safest way to do that?
expected_behavior: Does not read the github skill: skill_read is false
Answers with local git only (interactive rebase or git reset --soft, plus a safety branch or reflog escape hatch) and does not route the task through gh, pull requests or GitHub settings
Does not treat the request as a GitHub Actions, pull-request or repository-governance task
